terms.meaning: the hidden identifier stored for an option, separate from the label the user reads

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Trigger and scroll arrows
sections.what: Creates the box that shows the current choice and the up and down arrows for long lists.
sections.why: Likely reason: arrows tell the user that more items are above or below.
sections.watch_out: The trigger's height and width come from class names, so long chosen labels are cut short.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Dropdown panel and list area
sections.what: Creates the floating panel that holds the list and the scrolling area inside it, placed relative to the trigger.
sections.why: Likely reason: the popper mode keeps the list beside the box, which is the usual expectation.
sections.watch_out: The placement mode is set by a prop, and changing it moves the list and may need style changes.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Items, labels and dividers
sections.what: Creates each option row with a check mark when chosen, plus group headings and divider lines, and exports them.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is the standard look for dropdown rows.
sections.watch_out: The check mark sits on the right, so long item text can crowd it.

summary: Provides a dropdown where the user picks one value from a list, styled to match the app.
purpose: Lets screens offer a list of options in a compact box.
why: Likely reason: it wraps a library that handles keyboard and touch selection and adds the app's styling.
how: A trigger shows the current choice with a down arrow. When opened, a content panel lists the items, with up and down arrows for long lists. Group labels and dividers can be placed between items. The chosen item shows a check mark.
inputs: Options as children, the selected value and a change handler, and a position setting (popper by default).
outputs: A dropdown that shows one chosen value.
risks: The list panel floats in a portal, so it can be covered by other layers. Item values must be non-empty strings, as the underlying library does not accept empty ones.
debug: If the chosen value does not display, check the value passed to the root matches an item value exactly.
